description: From the Mirador de Orellán the ruined peaks of Las Médulas rise as dark silhouettes under the starry night, their reddish crests catching faint moonlight. Two thousand years after the Romans wrecked these mountains with hydraulic mining — ruina montium, the largest open-pit gold mine of the empire — the chestnut woods and ravines lie in complete darkness below. It is a naturally dark subject: no lighting is invented, and the UNESCO-listed landscape reads as a quiet black relief against the night sky.
